title: Knowledge check: Browser Compatibility and Support

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of browser compatibility and support?
options: Compatibility work begins with the official upgrade guide, a dependency inventory, tests, and a controlled migration plan. Do not teach removed APIs as current jQuery 4 functionality.
Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: Compatibility work begins with the official upgrade guide, a dependency inventory, tests, and a controlled migration plan. Do not teach removed APIs as current jQuery 4 functionality.
questions.explanation: Compatibility work begins with the official upgrade guide, a dependency inventory, tests, and a controlled migration plan. Do not teach removed APIs as current jQuery 4 functionality. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying reviewing official browser support?
options: Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use reviewing official browser support deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use reviewing official browser support deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with browser compatibility and support?
options: Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
